title: Spectral Residuals and Latent Recursion
subtitle: AIMuon · MoLR · RetNet
intro: Two main reads change spectral update directions and LoRA computation depth. Briefs cover local-update scaling, language information structure, inference budgets and one substantive revision. The RetNet classic derives equivalent parallel, recurrent and chunkwise forms.
window: November 20–23, 2026 (America/New_York; emphasis on updates since the previous issue, with a 72-hour overlap)

articles.paper: Accelerating Muon with Spectral Residual Correction
articles.authors: Ren, Zhixin · Lyu, Yao · Li, Shengbo Eben · Zhang, Liping
articles.title: AIMuon: polarize momentum and residual separately

blocks.text: AIMuon retains EMA momentum and corrects the parameter step using the current gradient–momentum residual. Let P(A) be the compact-SVD polar factor, with P(0)=0. Spectral–nuclear duality makes a linear subproblem with a squared spectral penalty produce nuclear-norm-weighted directions. [1]

blocks.label: The paper’s exact, unnormalized direction; the parameter step is −ηU. Separate polar transformations generally differ from polarizing a mixture.

blocks.label: The implementation applies five NS steps to each component, then matches the combined Frobenius norm to same-momentum Muon. Common scale disappears while relative weighting remains.

blocks.text: Pretraining uses 8×H100 from scratch and 524,288 tokens per step. Learning rates and momentum are tuned independently for each optimizer. The table reports interpolated step reductions to Muon’s final validation loss along full-budget curves. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The stationarity bound concerns the exact, unnormalized iteration, not the full NS/RMS-matched implementation. At equal token budgets, medium and Qwen training time rises about 5.6% and 4.2%, excluding validation. Fewer steps do not establish end-to-end speedups. [1]

articles.paper: Mixture of Latent Recursions for Low-Rank Adaptation
articles.authors: Luo, Weixun · Mao, Ye · Huang, Ranran · Jing, Junpeng · Mikolajczyk, Krystian
articles.title: MoLR: share a low-rank transform and allocate depth per token

blocks.text: A shared transform W sits between LoRA’s down-projection z₀=Ax and up-projection B. A router decides whether each token continues. Failing a threshold stops that token permanently, rather than allowing later reactivation. [2]

blocks.label: The paper’s active-token update; φ is a fixed step encoding. A stopped token retains its current state as its final representation.
The paper’s routing balance targets uniform stopping depths 0,…,T; q is conditional continuation probability. Additional parameters do not grow with maximum recursion depth T.

blocks.text: Worst-case additional MACs relative to LoRA are T(r+1)/(d_in+d_out). Varying the inference cap within the trained horizon yields a quality–computation tradeoff. This is not parameter-count scaling or a guarantee beyond trained depths. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Omitting step encodings gives an input-dependent polynomial in W; this simplified expansion is not the full algorithm with φ. Threshold balancing does not guarantee compute-optimal allocation for every example. [2]

articles.paper: $\mathtt{DistP}$: Scaling Local-Update Training with Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer
articles.authors: Jovanović, Andrej · Iacob, Alex · Wiesner, Philipp · Roux, Christophe · Zimmer, Max · Sani, Lorenzo · Pokutta, Sebastian · Lane, Nicholas D.
articles.title: DistP: hyperparameter transfer for local updates

blocks.text: Larger local batches and more workers follow different inner-learning-rate rules: the abstract reports square-root scaling and a fixed reference rate, plus fitted compute scaling. With outer momentum, changing batch size or synchronization intervals may still require joint inner–outer tuning. Full text was not read; no theorem is expanded and relative loss reductions are not treated as training speedups. [3]

articles.paper: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
articles.authors: Lufkin, Leon · Dawes, Cutter · Krishnamurthy, Kamesh
articles.title: Self-similar organization of predictive information

blocks.text: Mutual information between adjacent text windows and contextual band gains probe length scaling while avoiding an unknown entropy rate. The theory and experiments report collapse across lengths. This is evidence about language statistics and learnable long-context structure, not a universal parameter–compute scaling law. [4]

articles.title: Inference budgets for heterogeneous theorem provers

blocks.text: A predict-and-verify framework allocates budget across heterogeneous LLM solvers, within the inference-compute-allocation subscription. Abstract only: no transferable scaling exponent for arbitrary reasoning tasks is inferred. [5]

articles.paper: Power-Law Spectrum of the Random Feature Model
articles.authors: Paquette, Elliot · Xiao, Ke Liang · Zhu, Yizhe
articles.title: Random-feature spectra: from monomials to polynomials
articles.dateNote: First posted March 15, 2026; v2: November 19, 2026 ET
articles.evidence: Compared old abstract and relevant revised-text passages

blocks.text: Comparing the v1 abstract with v2 text verifies an extension from monomial to polynomial activations using Gaussian integration by parts. Gaussian inputs, covariance eigenvalues of order j^(−α), and α>1 remain crucial; this is not a spectral-preservation theorem for arbitrary nonlinearities or deep networks. [6]

classic.title: One retention operator, three execution orders
classic.paper: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
classic.authors: Yutao Sun · Li Dong · Shaohan Huang · Shuming Ma · Yuqing Xia · Jilong Xue · Jianyong Wang · Furu Wei
classic.dateNote: Historical preprint (2023); first posted July 17, 2023; read v4: August 9, 2023

recognition.label: 1,145 citations in the queried OpenAlex record (November 23, 2026)

classic.question: With fixed state capacity, how would a controlled long-range key–value retrieval experiment distinguish exponential forgetting from interference between memory writes?

blocks.text: Linear attention (2020) and S4 (2022) explored parallel training and fixed-state recurrence. RetNet (2023) introduces exponentially decayed retention. The core is three execution forms of one operator, not an exact RNN rewrite of softmax attention. [7]

blocks.label: The paper’s recurrent–parallel equivalence: q and k are row vectors, v is a value vector, and positional rotations are absorbed into q and k. For one head, 0<γ<1. Unrolling the recurrence gives the sum.
The paper’s parallel form, without softmax. Parallelizability does not make this explicit N×N implementation linear-time.

Index restatement of the paper’s chunkwise form: blocks have length B, with within-block parallelism and state R passed between blocks. Including the displayed decay powers, all three forms agree in exact arithmetic.
The paper’s multi-scale retention uses fixed head-specific decays, headwise normalization and gating. Residuals, pre-LayerNorm and FFNs also remain; the full network is not a single linear system.

blocks.text: At fixed width and layer count, each head caches a d_k×d_v recurrent matrix, independent of sequence length N. Cost still grows with width and batch size. Section 3 throughput comparisons depend on model, length, hardware and implementation; this note does not extrapolate their multipliers to modern optimized attention kernels. [7]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Read Sections 2–3. Algebraic equivalence does not guarantee identical floating-point errors, training gradients or engineering throughput. Fixed state removes cache growth without guaranteeing equivalence to a full KV cache on arbitrary long-range retrieval. [7]
